summary: API gateway backpressure mesh misconfiguration caused sudden 502 cliff under mixed embed/chat traffic
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 15:40 UTC BrightMaps reported a sharp increase in 502 responses from the Redwood API when sending mixed embedding + chat requests. The error pattern was a steep cliff of 502s lasting ~18 minutes, followed by a gradual decline.
impact: Customer-facing failures for BrightMaps internal analytics pipeline and chat assistant. Approximately 70% of requests returned 502 for a 18-minute window; error spike impacted SLAs and caused job retries and downstream timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a blended workload: 50% small embedding batch uploads (multi-part upload) + 50% chat generate calls with streaming enabled to BrightMaps tenant token.
2) Configure concurrency to match peak (tenant concurrency ~= 120) and observe 502 rate at API gateway and increased upstream runtime exits.
3) Confirm reproduction only when ingress-mesh backpressure multiplier is enabled on canary routes.
logs: apigw: 2026-03-12T15:41:02Z - upstream returned 502, upstream: runtime-proxy-7f6c (502 Bad Gateway)
runtime: 2026-03-12T15:41:05Z - worker-12 SIGTERM from watchdog during prefetched-kv lock hold; nvml logs show no OOM; nvml reset absent
ingress-mesh: 2026-03-12T15:40:58Z - backpressure_multiplier: 8.0 applied to route tenant/brightmaps (expected <=2.0)
grafana: panels: apigw_502_rate spike to 720/min, upstream_restart_count +40 in window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor causing GPU OOMs. Rejected after NVML and runtime memory metrics show no OOM or GPU resets.

Correlation found between a canary rollout of ingress-mesh weighting (backpressure smoothing v2) and start of error cliff. Canary configuration accidentally applied to production route 'tenant/brightmaps' via automated route-migration script.

Observed that smoothing algorithm amplified short-term accept-queue oscillations: it increased backpressure multiplier aggressively when accept-queue latency rose, which starved prefetch/keepalive handshakes and caused hedged retries from API gateway leading to upstream restart cascade.
Stack traces show runtime threads blocked on kv-prefetch lock for >6s followed by watchdog SIGTERM; worker exits caused apigw to surface 502s.
Related timeframe cross-checked with Slack thread #infra-deploy (thread ts 1678617600) and canary PR  https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-mesh/pull/892 linked below.

root_cause_summary: A canary configuration for the ingress-mesh backpressure smoothing algorithm was accidentally rolled out to a production tenant route. The smoothing logic over-amplified short accept-queue latency spikes (multiplier jumped to 8x), starving prefetch/keepalive handshakes, which triggered hedged retries and blocked runtime prefetched-kv locks leading to watchdog-initiated worker exits and a surface of 502s at the API gateway.
resolution: Immediate: rolled back canary smoothing v2 from tenant route and disabled automated route-migration. Customer workaround: recommended client-side exponential backoff and reduced hedged-retry burst. Next steps: patch smoothing logic to cap multiplier and add safer canary targeting checks. Change rolled out to canary and scheduled fix PR + canary verification.
postmortem_actions: 1) Engineering to implement multiplier hard-cap and hysteresis in smoothing algorithm (assigned INT-90110).
2) Add preflight check in automated route-migration to prevent canary flag drift (PR referenced).
3) Create an alert that maps sudden multiplier delta > 3x to automatic throttled rollback.
4) Customer follow-up call and shared runbook for retry/backoff guidance.
